To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the risk factors of (1) lack of project management experience, (2) lack of project manager experience, (3) lack of project team experience, (4) poor project team communication, (5) lack of project planning, and (6) lack of project control have significantly higher levels of risk effect on longer duration virtual projects.

the longer duration virtual projects, the higher risk factors are, especially for: project scope, project team members, project manager, project team member skills and abilities, project team member motivation and commitment, and project team member communications.

the following six risks are more significant on longer duration projects: (1) lack of a clear and complete project plan; (2) lack of a well-defined project scope; (3) lack of project management experience; (4) lack of a clearly defined project manager role; (5) lack of a formal change control process; and (6) lack of a project management methodology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of risk factors on virtual projects and the relationship between project duration, risk, and risk management.
the risk factors that threaten the success of virtual projects, and how the impact of these risk factors is influenced by the duration of the project.
identifying risk factors that have the highest impact on project duration.

the duration effect is not consistent across the entire set of risk factors.
project duration is a significant factor in the management of risk in virtual projects.
the duration of a project is one of the factors that determines how risky a project is.

project duration and the associated increased complexity, uncertainty, and time constraints, are important factors that must be considered in risk analysis and management of virtual projects.
the longer duration of the project, the more risk there is for the project to be in trouble.
